FISCAL SPONSORSHIP AGREEMENT (MODEL A — COMPREHENSIVE)

This Fiscal Sponsorship Agreement (this "Agreement") is made as of April 14, 2026 between Harborview Community Foundation, an Ohio nonprofit corporation exempt from federal income tax under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code and classified as a public charity under Section 509(a)(1) (the "Sponsor"), and the Sycamore Ridge Literacy Initiative, an unincorporated project (the "Project").

RECITALS

The Sponsor's charitable and educational purposes include supporting adult literacy in Franklin County. The Project's activities further those purposes. The parties intend a comprehensive (Model A) fiscal sponsorship, in which the Project becomes a program of the Sponsor rather than a separate legal entity, and no partnership, joint venture, or agency relationship is created between them.

1. THE PROJECT BECOMES A PROGRAM OF THE SPONSOR. The Sponsor accepts the Project as its own program. The Project has no separate legal existence. All assets, liabilities, income, and expenses of the Project are those of the Sponsor.

2. VARIANCE POWER. The Sponsor retains complete discretion and control over the use of all funds it receives for the Project, including the unilateral right to redirect those funds to other charitable purposes consistent with the Sponsor's exempt purposes, as Treasury Regulation § 1.170A-9(f)(11)(v)(B) requires and as the Sponsor's governing documents provide. No donor may impose a condition that would limit that power, and no representation to the contrary may be made to any donor.

3. CHARITABLE PURPOSE LIMITATION. Project funds may be used only for charitable, educational, and other purposes described in Section 170(c)(2)(B) of the Internal Revenue Code. No part of the net earnings may inure to the benefit of any private individual. No substantial part of the Project's activities may consist of attempting to influence legislation, and the Project may not participate in any political campaign on behalf of or in opposition to any candidate for public office.

4. FUNDS AND ACCOUNTING. The Sponsor will maintain the Project's funds in a restricted fund on its books, will account for them separately, and will include them in the Sponsor's audited financial statements and Form 990. The Sponsor is the recipient of all grants and contributions and issues all donor acknowledgments required by Section 170(f)(8).

5. ADMINISTRATIVE FEE. The Sponsor will retain an administrative fee of eight percent (8%) of all funds received for the Project, assessed on receipt.

6. PROJECT DIRECTOR AND EMPLOYEES. The Project Director serves at the pleasure of the Sponsor's Executive Director. Any person working on the Project is an employee or contractor of the Sponsor, not of the Project, and is subject to the Sponsor's personnel policies.

7. GRANT COMPLIANCE. The Sponsor is responsible for compliance with every grant agreement it enters for the Project, including reporting, and the Project will supply the Sponsor with the information and records the Sponsor needs.

8. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY. All intellectual property created in the course of the Project is owned by the Sponsor. On a transfer under Section 10, the Sponsor will assign it to the Successor.

9. TERM AND TERMINATION. This Agreement continues until terminated. Either party may terminate on sixty (60) days' written notice. The Sponsor may terminate immediately if continuing would jeopardize its exempt status or violate law.

10. TRANSFER ON TERMINATION. On termination, the Sponsor will, subject to its variance power and to the approval of its Board, transfer the Project's restricted fund balance and assets to a successor nonprofit corporation exempt under Section 501(c)(3) and classified as a public charity, chosen by the Sponsor after consulting the Project (the "Successor"). If no qualified Successor is identified within ninety (90) days, the Sponsor will devote the balance to its own charitable purposes consistent with the donors' intent, and no balance will be distributed to any individual.

11. NO PRIVATE BENEFIT. Nothing in this Agreement may be construed to confer a private benefit on any individual or to permit the Sponsor to act inconsistently with its exempt purposes.

12. INDEMNIFICATION. The Project Director and the Project's volunteers are covered by the Sponsor's directors' and officers' and general liability policies on the same terms as the Sponsor's other programs.

13. GOVERNING LAW. Ohio law governs this Agreement.

HARBORVIEW COMMUNITY FOUNDATION            SYCAMORE RIDGE LITERACY INITIATIVE
